title: A Judgment of God
text: A JUDGMENT OF GOD.-It was upon one of these occasions, when Jeroboam stood by his altar at Beth-el, that God sent a prophet from Judea to rebuke the idolatrous monarch, and to predict the overthrow of that very altar, by a prince of David's line called Josias. Jeroboam, incensed at the insolence of the speaker, stretched out his hand to arrest him, but he had scarcely done so when the arm withered, and he was to draw it back. Alarmed, rather than conscience-struck by the judgment, Jeroboam entreated the prophet to pray for him, which was done, and the use of his arm restored; but the king took no further notice of the prophet's rebuke, except by inviting him to his house with the promise of a reward. This however the stranger declined, declaring that God had positively forbidden him to eat or drink within the bounds of the impious kingdom, and that even to return by the way which he had followed in coming was prohibited. He accordingly mounted his ass, and leaving the assembly to think what they might, took a new direction homewards.
